llm.summary: This is a coherent Canonry operations guide with broad, sensitive integrations, but the risky actions are disclosed and generally bounded by approval and server-side permission checks.

dimensions.detail: Local config and connected integrations handle sensitive credentials and business data, including OAuth tokens, API keys, service-account files, WordPress application passwords, logs, and traffic samples. This is proportionate for Canonry administration, but users must protect the local credential store.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is Markdown documentation and references only; I found no executable install hook, packaged script, obfuscation, or hidden payload. Metadata is empty.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main guide repeatedly requires explicit approval for live provider calls, syncs, writes, and externally visible actions, and says credentials belong in private setup flows rather than chat. A feedback section should still be treated as requiring user awareness before sending reports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The docs disclose persistent local state, schedules, logs, agent conversations or memory, Cloudflare workers/queues, and sync jobs. These are product features and are operator-controlled rather than hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The top-level purpose fits Canonry operations, evidence review, diagnostics, integrations, and reporting; references also document high-impact workflows such as WordPress writes, OpenAI Ads campaign operations, Cloudflare traffic capture, schedules, and API-key management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you intend to operate Canonry. Use read-only or stored-only modes where possible, keep ~/.canonry/config.yaml and token/key files private, do not paste secrets into chat, and require explicit approval before writes, ad-spend actions, schedules, public webhooks, Cloudflare route changes, or WordPress content changes.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The required SKILL.md was fully present and inspected; referenced files are local Markdown references. I did not find evidence of analysis evasion.
[TM1] expected: The cited DELETE path is a documented project-scoped content-dismissal restore operation requiring write authority, not evidence of unsafe parameter abuse.
[EA5] expected: Provider/model settings are expected for Canonry setup and quota control; they are disclosed and require appropriate authority, though users should confirm billing and model choices.
[PE3] expected: The referenced API-key guidance is setup documentation for Bing and other integrations, not credential theft. Secrets should still be handled outside chat and kept private.
[RA2] expected: State files, schedules, logs, sync history, and agent sessions are disclosed Canonry features. I did not find hidden cron jobs or unauthorized persistence in the skill artifact.
[SQP-2] expected: Plaintext local credential storage in ~/.canonry/config.yaml is disclosed and expected for the CLI, but it is a real hygiene consideration; restrictive file permissions or secure secret storage would reduce risk.
[E1] expected: External calls to Bing, Cloudflare, Canonry receivers, and provider APIs match the documented indexing, traffic, and integration workflows. I did not find unrelated exfiltration instructions.
[EA3] expected: The CLI reference is broader than the short front-matter summary, but it is presented as optional host-native reference material and repeatedly directs agents to read only task-relevant sections.
[AIG-SARIF] expected: The supplied static scan reported no results.
